name: Upwork proposal: short personalized proof + single CTA
goal: Write Upwork cover letters that avoid archive-bait mistakes and follow a tight pattern: client first name, brief proof/social proof, one CTA to book a call, skim-friendly P.S., and prior ToS literacy.

source.title: Upwork Proposals: 8 Golden Rules for Writing Upwork Cover Letters

constraints: Operational freelancing/product procedure only — no get-rich-quick claims.
Ground every step in YouTube-provided captions; adapt UI labels if the product renamed menus.
No question-dump in the first proposal.
Don't name a direct competitor client; say you've worked with another client in the space.

steps.action: Avoid archive bait: generic salutation, false 'I fully understand', leading with inexperience, empty promises, ignoring requested example counts, unsolicited full drafts, packing questions into the proposal.
Personalize with client first name (often in feedback history); optionally Google the business for industry context.
Keep it short; establish authority with a profile client quote or concrete proof.
One CTA only: book a call (questions happen on the call/scheduling form).
Add a P.S. — skimmers often read it even when they skip links.
Before serious bidding, read Upwork Terms of Service fully; treat ToS literacy as required to get paid safely.
